subject: Unexpected mid-month usage spike — request for manual audit and retro credit
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@orbitai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbitAI Billing <billing@orbitai.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected mid-month spike — billing hold and audit request

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a sharp usage spike on our June 28 invoice (see attached screenshot) that we don't recognize — token counts jump ~8x for a 3-hour window. This pushed us over our committed tier and generated an overage charge. We only deployed a small model change earlier that day; nothing that should cause this magnitude of traffic.

Can you put the invoice on hold while we work through this? We'd also like Redwood to run a manual metering audit (request-level sampling / dedup check). If it helps, I can share a link to our request logs and sample request IDs.

OrbitAI is on a monthly post-pay plan. We're hoping for a retro credit if this turns out to be a metering anomaly. Please advise next steps and what evidence you need from us.

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of Engineering, OrbitAI
sam@orbitai.com
+1 415-555-0134

Attachment: orbit-usage-screenshot.png (image/png)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@orbitai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike — billing hold and audit request

Thanks for flagging this, Sam. Sorry to hear about the surprise — we'll pause collection on the disputed line item while we investigate (I won't cancel the invoice).

Next steps from our side:
- I'll open a manual metering audit with Ben (billing ops) and loop in Lauren for CS liaison.
- Could you send a 24-hour window of request-level logs (IDs + timestamps + model name + token counts) and mark a couple of representative request IDs? A cloud storage link is fine.
- Useful context: any batch jobs, migrations, retry logic, or webhook backfills that ran 6/28 02:00–06:00 UTC?

I'll propose a provisional credit while we validate. Ben — can you intake a billing_audit_request_form and confirm a provisional cap we can offer pending root-cause? Lauren — please add OrbitAI to the queue for a post-incident follow-up call.

Best,
Grace
Director, Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@orbitai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike — billing hold and audit request

Sam — thanks for the heads up and for the screenshot. I'm starting the manual audit now.

Ask from billing ops: please complete and return the attached billing_audit_request_form.pdf (one-page) so our team can accept the request formally. We'll need:
- Signed confirmation that OrbitAI authorizes Redwood to sample request-level logs.
- Preferred contact for any follow-up questions.

Provisional credit: we can provisionally reserve up to $2,000 of credit against the disputed charge while the audit runs. That will be applied to your account hold and reconciled after audit completion. If the audit finds usage was legitimate, we'll remove the temporary credit and invoice accordingly (we'll give 48 hours' notice).

Technical note for the audit team: look for duplicated request_ids, anomalous token inflation, and retry loops. If OrbitAI provides a GCS export link, please include it in the ticket.

Ben Carter
Billing Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: billing_audit_request_form.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Sam Patel <sam@orbitai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbitAI Billing <billing@orbitai.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike — billing hold and audit request

Ben, Grace — attaching the log export link and a small sample file. We dug into our infra and found a one-off migration job that launched a large batch of index rebuilds at 02:12 UTC on 6/28; due to a bug, the job retried on failure and ended up reissuing the same requests 3x over ~45 minutes.

Log export: https://storage.googleapis.com/orbit-exports/orbit-log-export-20260628.jsonl
Sample (first 10k lines) attached: orbit-log-export-20260628.jsonl

We completed and signed the billing_audit_request_form — see attached PDF. We accept the provisional credit while you confirm whether the retries were double-counted by Redwood metering.

Sam

Attachment: orbit-log-export-20260628.jsonl (application/jsonl)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@orbitai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month spike — billing hold and audit request

Sam — quick update and proposed resolution: our audit team sampled the export and confirmed that ~72% of the additional token volume during the window was attributable to duplicate requests that should have been deduplicated at ingest (retry loop). We will: 

1) Apply a retroactive credit of $1,350 to OrbitAI's June invoice (applied today).
2) Keep the provisional hold in place until you confirm the adjusted invoice; if you accept, we'll finalize and close the ticket.
3) Send a short postmortem with recommended guardrails (retry throttling, idempotency keys) and offer a 30-minute technical review with our infra team.

Please reply to accept the credit and we will finalize. If you prefer escalation to legal for a different remedy, tell us and we'll coordinate.

Thanks for the speedy cooperation. Lauren will follow up to schedule the review.

— Grace
Director, Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
